:::{#thm-joint-distribution-rectangles}
#### A joint distribution is determined by its rectangle probabilities

If [jointly distributed](#def-jointly-distributed) random variables $\Xin$,
and jointly distributed random variables $\dsn{Y}$,
satisfy

$$\Pr(X_1 \in A_1, \ldots, X_n \in A_n) = \Pr(Y_1 \in A_1, \ldots, Y_n \in A_n)$$

for all sets $\dsn{A}$ of real numbers for which these are events,
then $(\Xin)$ and $(\dsn{Y})$ have the same [joint distribution](#def-joint-distribution).

:::
